title: How WorldCom Turned $3.8 Billion in Costs Into "Investments"

lines.say: WorldCom's biggest expense was line costs, the fees it paid to use other telephone networks.
In two thousand one, prosecutors said, the company started booking part of them as capital expenditures, like new equipment.
lines.show: In 2001, prosecutors said, the company started booking part of them as capital expenditures, like new equipment.

lines.say: At a dinner, the CFO told CEO Bernard Ebbers the first move, over five hundred million dollars, wasn't right. Ebbers did not stop him.
lines.show: At a dinner, the CFO told CEO Bernard Ebbers the first move, over $500 million, "wasn't right." Ebbers did not stop him.

lines.say: Quarter by quarter: seven hundred seventy-one million, more than six hundred ten million, more than seven hundred million, more than nine hundred forty-one million, eight hundred eighteen million.
lines.show: Quarter by quarter: $771 million, more than $610 million, more than $700 million, more than $941 million, $818 million.
